paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the truth about Jesus can sit in plain sight and still get handed around like paperwork. Festus walked in expecting crimes. What he got were arguments about their own religion and "a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive" (Acts 25:19). Festus said he was "at a loss as to how to investigate these matters" (Acts 25:20).

And look at what the whole room could hear. Festus told them he "found he had done nothing worthy of death" (Acts 25:25), and he had nothing definite to write to the Emperor about Paul (Acts 25:26). The whole Jewish community was crying out that Paul "ought not to live any longer" (Acts 25:24), and still Festus found nothing worthy of death. Paul stood there with one message at the center of it all: Jesus is alive.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Faith in Jesus doesn't need a crowd cheering or a king clapping. Paul stood in a hall full of pomp, and the thing at the center of his case was the truth about Jesus. Hold that truth steady like that, and let it stand on its own. This story isn't over, because Paul is about to speak.
